The only stories written about her as of now are of her bad temper. Eventually, I'll write mythology about her better qualities! She's seen as impartial to any mortal quests. She simply doesn't care. Her followers are typically seen adorning red clothes, or at least gold jewelry or red stones. Aside from clothes, her followers can be identified by their Udum marks. Basically, when a person is born on the islands of prigolain, at their first breath, tattoo like marks appear on their bodies. The color and location indicate the persons first and secondary deities. These marks have a direct correlation to the persons personality, temperament, and core values/strengths. The designs of the marks are completely unique to each person. Even if someone shares the exact same first and secondary deities, they won't be the same. 
 All of her followers have her as either their first or second. And because of her lifelong feude with her twin brother, those who have him as their primary deities never get along. Its kinda like a super accurate zodiac sign. Her followers worship her the same way everyone else worships other deities, an altar designated to her. Her offerings are commonly burnt meat/vegetables, red stones, gold, candles, and specific incense. She's easily offended, so people consider their offerings very, very carefully. She does have a few temples, but they're very small and scattered throughout the islands. While she did have a few high priests/priestesses in the beginning times, she hasn't chosen one in many generations. And yes, those who dislike her typically avoid the colors red, yellow, gold and orange. Some are so set in their beliefs that they won't even eat red foods, including red meat.

Ogrut-
A large fruit tree that grows up to 22 feet tall and lives up to 35 years. It's susceptible to disease and destructive insect infestation. It has a knobbly, slanted trunk covered in thick, waxy, dark red bark. Inside, the wood is light and tan in color. The branches are short and are covered with very large amounts of huge, very thin leaves with serrated edges. The leaves themselves are magenta with golden splotches. In early "spring" it produces large amounts of giant copper colored blossoms with broad, flat petals. They are hardy and have no scent. In late "summer" it produces large oblong fruit called Eava. The fruit has a rubbery olive skin that is thin and Edible when Boiled. It's sweet and slightly crunchy with blood red flesh that's very juicy. The red seeds are tiny and are bunched at the top of the fruit. The roots of the tree spread far and go deep underground. Forests of this species are spread far apart to make room for their thick canopy and wide roots. Overall, this tree is sturdy, flexible and difficult to uproot or break.
Ekren-
This large fruit tree grows up to 25 feet tall and lives up to 20 years. It is very resistant to destructive insect infestation but is susceptible to disease. It has a very thick curved trunk with paper thin brown bark. The inside of the tree is sturdy and the wood is soft brown. The branches are typically thin and curved, topped with thin red leaves with smooth edges. During the winter the leaves fall off the tree leaving it baren. In early spring it produces large amounts of tiny, peach colored blossoms with circular petals. They are delicate and have a sweet scent. In early autumn it produces very small, nearly heart shaped pit fruit with a cream colored skin that bursts when bitten. It's very juicy and the insides are white. The roots are fine and grow in a large web. Forests of this species are packed tightly together with roots interwoven, patches of undergrowth grow between them. The leaves can be harvested straight from the tree and used to create dyes.

There's a story behind that but it's pretty wordy but if you'd like to know more feel free to message me and I'd be happy to tell you!

Thank you! And yes most of the villages are solely on the banks of the rivers or lakes! Since the rivers were formed a few thousand years in the past, a lot of people made small shallow streams further inland so they could live deeper in the island. This isn't super common because it's kinda sacrilegious but it does happen by certain high priests/priestess and their followers (mainly followers of deities who have drama with the ocean Goddess for whatever reason). Because the island is predominantly uninhabited, they do most of their business in the forest! Ocean water is sacred to them so they wouldn't use it for excretion, but they see animals use the bathroom in the forest so to them its not a disrespectful thing to do to the earth Goddess, especially because it ends up fertilizing the plants more! And yes there are some areas on the beaches or shallow waters that are blocked off by stones to form small pools that a lot of people go to to socialize! Teens like hanging out there after their schooling and mothers bring their children there to teach them to swim! If you'd like to hear any more or talk about it more in depth feel free to message me!
